  C.  Malibu Library Set Aside Funds for Fiscal Year 2024-2025

  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council concerning
  the use of the Malibu Library Set Aside Funds for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  Deputy City Manager Brown provided an overview of the agenda report including
  the proposed funding requests provided by the Los Angeles County Library staff
  which includes potential staffing changes, a security guard, and an updated
  feasibility study. Deputy City Manager Brown also stated that the library will work
  with the County CEO’s Department to bring the library to dark sky ordinance
  compliance.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that Malibu Library Set Aside Funds are not to be
  used for dark sky ordinance compliance.

  Deputy City Manager Brown continued her presentation and stated that staff
  received and submitted as part of the meeting record funding requests from Malibu
  High School for $44,000 and Malibu Elementary School for $40,000. She presented
  the spending plan and provided details regarding budgeting actuals and variances.

  Councilmember Riggins opened up the floor for public comment.

  Kasey Earnest spoke in favor of appropriating funds for the Boys and Girls Club to
  be used for supplies and to support the Director of Education.

  Harriet Pollon spoke in favor of appropriating funds for Friends of the Library to
  be used for signs guiding people to the library.

  Andrew White spoke in favor of appropriating funds for Malibu Elementary School
  to be used for the nonfiction and T-K sections. He also requested funds on behalf
  of Perry Monte from Webster Library.

  Patrick Miller spoke in favor of appropriating funds for Malibu High School to be
  used for printing machines.

  Councilmember Riggins closed public comment.

  Councilmembers Riggins and Silverstein asked for clarifying questions from the
  applicants

  Community Library Manager Melissa Stallings clarified the day-to-day use of
  funds.

  Deputy City Manager Brown stated that a library nexus must be present in order to
  approve the use of the Malibu Library Set Aside Funds.

  Councilmember Silverstein encouraged schools not to be conservative in their fund
  requests so long as the nexus is present.

  Councilmember Riggins agreed and inquired if outreach has been made to Our
  Lady of Malibu (OLM) to ensure they know of these funds.

  Community Library Manager Stallings stated that they do not have a library but
  they do bring their classes to the library.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that ideally a large portion of the funds would be
  used for capital improvement projects.

  Councilmember Silverstein agreed and stated that he would like to see a robust
  library center or possibly a performing arts center.

  Councilmember Riggins inquired about the possibility of moving the entrance to
  the front of the building.

  Councilmember Silverstein shared that the entrance could be studied by a
  consultant but agreed that signage should be included in the fund request.

  Councilmember Riggins inquired regarding the need for shade.

  Community Library Manager Stallings stated that the patio furniture gets used
  heavily, however, shared that a shade structure would need a lot of maintenance.
  She stated that they don’t receive complaints regarding the lack of shade on the
  patio.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired about the use of the patio.
 Malibu Library Subcommittee

  Community Library Manager Stallings stated that everyone who visits the library
  can use the space, housed or unhoused, she stated that to use the space one must
  enter through the library.

  Councilmember Silverstein stated that he was inclined to not approve funding for
  patio furniture until more information is provided about who is using it.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that the City Council can make this decision as they
  are both split on providing funds to replace the patio furniture at the library. She
  also stated that she would like to see a more detailed request from Webster
  Elementary School.

  Councilmember Silverstein encouraged Ms. Earnest to consider requesting
  additional funds from the Library Set Aside Funds instead of split between the
  Annual City’s General Fund Grants which could potentially open up funding for
  other organizations.

  Ms. Earnest stated that they provide broad resources, for example, services to their
  aging population, and added that she would like to ensure a library nexus.

  Councilmember Riggins inquired about what kind of services are available to the
  west side and shared that she would like to see what services are desired on the west
  side.

  Deputy City Manager Brown stated that the feasibility study would need to include
  an outreach component to determine the services desired.

  Councilmember Silverstein added that he would like to explore using already
  existing buildings and focusing on expansion as opposed to acquiring land for a
  state-of-the-art library.

  Councilmember Riggins inquired about the types of programming already offered.

  Community Library Manager Stallings stated that they have cooking and gardening
  programs.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired about the need for a water bottle filling station.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that she was very in favor of having these stations
  and pointed out how they are available at City Hall.

  Councilmember Silverstein stated that the Malibu Film Society request can be
  removed as they are looking for a more appropriate venue. He stated that since the
  special education programs are also being pulled if there was still a need for a
  special projects librarian.

  Councilmember Riggins recommended keeping the position in the budget if
  potential programs are established.

  Councilmember Silverstein inquired about the reasoning for a consultant need
  versus staff time being dedicated to this outreach.

  City Manager McClary clarified that staff already have a full plate and would need
  to re-prioritize certain projects to create space for this type of outreach. He stated
  that he is very conscious about getting projects beyond research and into
  implementation.

  Councilmember Riggins inquired about the maintenance line item and asked for
  more details about the HVAC replacement.

  Community Library Manager Stallings stated that this is something that came up in
  the needs assessment.

  Councilmember Riggins recommended evaluating the HVAC system and to
  consider scheduling a replacement.

CONSENSUS  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a
  motion to approve as amended, subject to changes including a line item of $100,000
  for schools, remove the Malibu Film Society request, allow the City Council to
  decide on patio furniture, changes to the language regarding the second librarian,
  and include discretion to increase funding for Boys and Girls Club. The question
  was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

Subject:  Malibu Library Set Aside Funds for Fiscal Year 2025-2026

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council regarding a prioritized
list of issues to be discussed at the yearly meeting between the City and County Library to discuss
the use of the Malibu Library Set Aside Funds for Fiscal Year 2025-2026.

FISCAL IMPACT: There is no fiscal impact on the city with this action. Malibu Public Library
services are paid for from a designated portion of property tax. Every year the County of Los
Angeles sets aside the difference between the property tax dollars apportioned to the County
Library from property within the City of Malibu and the Malibu Library expenses into a designated
fund. The ending balance for Set Aside Funds as of FY 22-23 totaled approximately $21.9 million;
this includes a surplus of $2.6 million; an updated ending balance for Malibu Library Set Aside
Funds for FY 23-24 was not available at the time this report was published.

DISCUSSION: In November of each year, the City and County Library staff are to meet to discuss
the Malibu Library Set Aside Fund and the use of Set Aside Funds for the following fiscal year. In
preparation for this meeting, the Malibu Library Subcommittee is asked to make a
recommendation to the City Council regarding a prioritized list of issues to be discussed at the
yearly meeting in accordance with the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the
County of Los Angeles and the City of Malibu.

Background

The Malibu Library was established in 1970 by the County of Los Angeles and is located on the
county-owned civic center property. In September 2008, the city and county executed an MOU
that governs the use of the Set Aside Funds. The MOU established a structure in which the
expenditure of the excess funds generated from the taxes that Malibu residents pay could be spent
on the Malibu Library. On March 26, 2018, the City and the County executed an amendment to the

  Page 1 of 3
  Agenda Item # 3.B.
 MOU extending the term until 2044, with two possible five-year extensions. All other terms remain
the same.

To optimize the allocation of local property tax dollars and provide the maximum benefit to the
Malibu community, the City has conducted two comprehensive library needs assessments in
collaboration with the County Library. The first needs assessment was completed in 2005, and the
Malibu Library Needs Assessment (2005 Needs Assessment) was approved by the City Council on
August 8, 2005. In 2024, the City Council also approved appropriating funds to conduct an updated
needs assessment.

In the past, Set Aside Funds have been used for the Malibu Library Speaker Series, to enhance
service hours, establish a deferred maintenance fund, hire additional library staff, hire a full-time
security guard, enhance library collections, materials and services, and support related services at
the Boys and Girls Club of Malibu and in Malibu public schools.

Malibu Library Set Aside Fund

It was previously estimated that approximately $1 million would be added to the Set Aside Fund
each year based on certain assumptions, including an estimated cost of living increase of 3%,
and did not take into account a change in the cost of the services being provided or a significant
increase or decrease in revenue. The ending balance for Set Aside Funds as of FY 22-23 totaled
approximately $21.9 million; this includes a surplus of $2.6 million.

As the Subcommittee considers its recommendations for the use of Set Aside Funds, it is
important to note that these funds must be used solely to improve or provide Malibu Library
facilities and services. The Library Subcommittee’s recommendations on the prioritized list of
issues to be discussed regarding the use of Set Aside Funds for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 will be
presented to the City Council for final approval prior to staff’s meeting with County Library Staff.
